sources.title: James N. Pratt Crew - 427th BS
sources.summary: The 303rd BG Association's page on the Pratt crew. Gives the 4 August 1943 loss of B-17F 42-3124 (427th BS, GN-N) on Arenig Fawr on a night cross-country training flight, the eight men killed, and the officers sent to recover them. Also covers the 1945 plaque, its 2019 replacement and rededication, and the 1996 plaque at Bala. Credits historian Harry D. Gobrecht and Richard Evans.

sources.summary: Article by Chaplain Capt. Hans Decker, published 13 September 2019 (live site 403; read via Wayback snapshot of 18 April 2026). Richard Evans and Councillor Dilwyn Morgan, Chairman of Gwynedd County Council, raised funds for a new memorial. Ten airmen from RAF Croughton joined RAF personnel and local people for the rededication on 4 September 2019.

paragraphs.text: Flying Fortress 42-3124 belonged to the 427th Bomb Squadron, 303rd Bomb Group, and had been at Molesworth since June 1943. Most sources call it a B-17F, but IWM's register calls it a B-17G. On the night of 3 August 1943 it took off at 23:54 on a cross-country training flight. At 01:00 on 4 August it flew into Arenig Fawr, the mountain about six miles west of Bala.

There was no radio contact. Flying control at AAF Station 107 reported the bomber overdue at 02:50, and at 03:00 came word of an unknown aircraft down on the peak. The US accident report found it hit about 50 ft below the summit, carried on to the top and caught fire. Parachutes were found in the wreckage. The cause was given as flying into high ground.

All eight men on board were killed. The Home Guard took two hours to climb to the wreck and could do nothing because .50 calibre ammunition was exploding. The 427th's engineering officer, Capt Quentin Hargrove, and flight surgeon Capt Louis A. Lame were sent to investigate and recover the bodies.
Five of the eight were the regular crew of 1st Lt James N. Pratt. Sgt Walter B. Robinson, Sgt Phillip Simonte and PFC Alfred B. Van Dyke were not regular members of the crew.

Apart from the tail, the aircraft burnt out. Most of the wreckage was taken away by 34 Maintenance Unit and the 2nd Strategic Air Depot. Melted aluminium and small fragments remain on the slope, and the site is a Protected Place under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986.

The memorial is a plaque in the cairn on Moel yr Eglwys, the highest summit of Arenig Fawr. The prehistoric cairn is a Scheduled Ancient Monument, and its stones were later rebuilt around a trig pillar, two walkers' shelters and this memorial.

The 303rd Bomb Group Association and the US Air Force say local people put up the first plaque in 1945. Sources differ on its later history. Coflein says the summit plaque was replaced in 1983 after damage. IWM's register records a slate tablet unveiled on 4 August 1988, broken by 2010.

By 2019 the slate plaque had deteriorated badly. On 31 August 2019 a local team replaced it with a silicon bronze plaque of the same size and wording, after two years of planning by Richard Evans and Councillor Dilwyn Morgan. On 4 September 2019 it was dedicated by RAF and US Air Force personnel and local people. Coflein's 2025 visit describes the new plaque as brass.

The current plaque names all eight men with their home towns. Its opening reads: "In memory of the crew of the Flying Fortress which crashed on the Arenig Fawr 4th August 1943." Older records give shorter wording: IWM has "crashed on the Arenig" and War Memorials Online has "crashed into the Arenig on the night of the 4th August 1943". War Memorials Online lists seven names and leaves out 2nd Lt William A. Bowling.

There is a second plaque in Bala, placed in 1996. The 303rd Bomb Group Association says it went up on 23 May 1996 on the entrance wall of the Village Hall, given by the Village of Tinley Park, Illinois, home town of the navigator, 2nd Lt Allan M. Boner. Coflein places it on the Old Town Hall.

For many years a group of Bala people climbed the mountain to lay a wreath at the memorial. The 2019 replacement was planned by Richard Evans and Councillor Dilwyn Morgan, who led the fundraising. No source names a body that looks after the memorial today.

notes:
NO MEMORIAL RECORD YET: public/data/memorials/arenig-fawr-b-17-42-3124.json does not exist, so the CLI validate reports 'no memorial record with this id'. Per instructions I did not create it. validate() itself passes (checked by calling the function directly).

AI SUMMARY CHECK (Steve Davis's pasted Google-AI-style text). Each item was checked against fetched sources:
- 427th BS / 303rd BG: CONFIRMED (303rd BGA, AAM, Coflein).
- Molesworth: CONFIRMED (AAM, USAF 501st CSW article). BBC says 'Mossley Hill Airbase in Cambridgeshire'. That is recorded as a conflicting station claim (C7). A secondary-only version can't be shown in a publishable paragraph, so the narrative uses AAM's assignment event (C28) for the base and leaves the BBC version in the claims and these notes. Coflein's accident summary says 'AAF Station 107'; I did not claim that is Molesworth.
- Night training flight: CONFIRMED (303rd BGA 'night cross-country training flight'; Coflein take-off 23:54, crash 01:00).
- 854 m summit: CONFIRMED by BBC only ('2,802ft (854m)'), secondary tier. 303rd BGA and USAF say 2,800 ft. Kept as an event claim, not in any paragraph.
- Local plaque 1945: CONFIRMED (303rd BGA, BBC, USAF/DVIDS). CONFLICTS with IWM (unveiled 4 Aug 1988) and Coflein (replaced 1983 after damage).
- Silicon bronze replacement: CONFIRMED (303rd BGA, BBC). Installed 31 Aug 2019 (303rd BGA). Coflein's 2025 visit calls it brass.
- Rededicated 4 Sept 2019 with RAF/USAF present: CONFIRMED (303rd BGA, USAF article, DVIDS caption, BBC preview).
- Wreckage ~330 yards from the plaque: NOT CONFIRMED. No source gives a distance from the plaque. Peak Wreck Hunters (community blog) says wreckage trails about 300 m down the slope. Coflein says melted aluminium where it burned out, with small fragments scattered down the slope. Left out.
- Bala Village Hall plaque 1996: CONFIRMED by 303rd BGA (entrance wall of Bala Village Hall, 23 May 1996, donated by Tinley Park, IL). Coflein says the face of the Old Town Hall, Bala, 1996. The two could be the same building under different names; not confirmed.

CONFLICTS RECORDED:
- Boner forename: Allan (plaque photo, AAM, Coflein, WMO) vs Allen (303rd BGA).
- Johnston vs Johnson: Johnston (plaque photo, 303rd BGA, WMO) vs Johnson (AAM aircraft text 'Walt Johnson', Coflein 'Walter J Johnson'). Coflein is institutional, so crosscheck resolves to Johnson by tier. But the plaque itself reads JOHNSTON, so a human should decide before apply.
- Johnston role: tail gunner (303rd BGA) vs flight engineer (AAM 'Flight engineer/top turret gunner', Coflein 'engineer').
- Royar: Frederic (plaque, 303rd, AAM, Coflein) vs Frederick (WMO). Rank: T/Sgt everywhere except WMO, which lists him as 2nd Lt. WMO's list has seven names and no Bowling, so it looks like Bowling's rank was attached to Royar. That is my reading, not a source.
- Simonte: Phillip (plaque, 303rd, Coflein) vs Philip (WMO); AAM 'Phil'.
- Robinson and Simonte role: waist gunner (AAM) vs gunner (Coflein). Not a real disagreement, but the tool flags it.
- Aircraft type: B-17F (303rd BGA, AAM 'B-17F-25-DL', Coflein accident report, WMO) vs B-17G (IWM WMR 13341 title). IWM is likely wrong, but it ties on tier with Coflein, so it is unresolved.
- Dedication date: 1945 (303rd BGA; BBC and USAF secondary) vs 1988-08-04 (IWM, institutional). Crosscheck resolves to 1988 by tier. A human should look at this: three independent publishers say the original went up in 1945. IWM's 1988 date may be a re-erection or replacement (cf. Coflein's '1983').
- Inscription: current plaque (reader photo, full text, 'ON THE ARENIG FAWR') vs IWM abbreviated ('ON THE ARENIG ... (Names)') vs WMO ('crashed into the Arenig on the night of the 4th August 1943', no 'crew of'). The older records probably describe the earlier slate plaque(s). 303rd BGA says the 2019 plaque copies the original's wording, which doesn't fit WMO's text. Unresolved.
- names_on_memorial: 8 (IWM, plaque photo) vs 7 (WMO, omits Bowling).
- Crew count: 8 in every source; no conflict. Crash date: 4 Aug 1943 in every source I read. A search-engine snippet attributed 8 Aug 1943 to the AAM, but the AAM page I read says 4/8/43. Peak Wreck Hunters gives the serial as 42-3134 (a typo; community tier, no claim made).

COORDINATES: there is no record field, so they are event claims C24-C27. Memorial: IWM map link 52.919353, -3.747558 (from IWM grid SH 82471 37109); WMO map 52.919052, -3.746335. These agree to about 100 m. Coflein summit cairn SH 82700 36950; Coflein crash site SH 82683 37165. The US accident report position as quoted by Coflein (52 54 08N, 03 44 03W, about 52.9022, -3.7342) is roughly 2 km south of the summit, so it is probably a wartime approximation; don't use it for the map. I had no grid-to-lat/long converter (no pyproj), so I could not check the Coflein grid refs against the IWM/WMO points myself. Recommended map point: IWM 52.919353, -3.747558.

HOME TOWNS: from the plaque photo only (researched-tier correspondence), except Boner's Tinley Park, which 303rd BGA also gives. A second publisher for the other seven was not found. AAM person pages for Royar, Van Dyke, Simonte and Johnston are behind Cloudflare and not archived. LEAD: argenweb.net Randolph County, Arkansas page (Lee & Betty Tucker, 2001) reproduces a local notice for 'Lt. J. N. Pratt', a heavy bomber pilot lost 4 Aug 1943, born Pocahontas, Arkansas, 15 June 1920, with his wife living in Boise, Idaho. It never names the aircraft or Wales, so linking it to this crash is inference. No claim made. If confirmed, Pratt's home town is Pocahontas, AR and Boise was his wife's home.

TIERS: AAM is IWM-run, but its aircraft history is a compiled summary, so I gave it 'researched', not 'institutional'. The Steve Davis correspondence is 'researched' because it is a photo of the plaque itself, evidence for the inscription and names. He is not the custodian, so it should not be used for anything beyond what the plaque shows. The DVIDS caption is marked copies_of the USAF article (identical caption text). The USAF article and AAM were read from Wayback snapshots because the live sites return 403.

CUSTODIAN: unknown. No source names a current custodian. WMO custodian fields are empty; IWM says sponsor type 'private'. Leads: Richard Evans and Councillor Dilwyn Morgan (2019 replacement organisers; named in that role by 303rd BGA, BBC and USAF, not as custodians), Bala Town Council, Cyngor Gwynedd, Eryri National Park (the summit is a Scheduled Ancient Monument, so Cadw consent may apply to any work). Not contacted, hence 'unknown', not 'unknown-confirmed'.

NOT FOUND / NOT CHECKED: ABMC (crew presumably repatriated; no burial found for any man), burial places, ages, service numbers for six men, Aviation Safety Network (403), Traces of War (403), Aircrew Remembered and Peak District Air Accident Research (no page found), the Doylerush 'No Landing Place' books cited by Coflein (not seen), the US accident report PDF on Coflein (not downloaded), a Geograph photo of the new plaque (not searched). The photo used is IWM's (Paul Newby), which shows the older slate plaque.
8 Nov 2026 rulings (Holly): Johnston per the plaque and 303rd BGA/WMO (AAM and Coflein spell Johnson). B-17F per four sources and AAM model B-17F-25-DL (IWM title says B-17G).
